dated.gap: Reaching a state of good repair across the eighteen infrastructure categories graded in 2025 requires $9.1 trillion, against $5.4 trillion of forecast investment, leaving a $3.7 trillion shortfall (ASCE Infrastructure Report Card)
dated.evidence: ASCE released the first Report Card for America's Infrastructure in 1998, establishing a national infrastructure investment gap as a recurring finding [web:42][web:46][web:50].
dated.orientationNote: ASCE is a professional engineering society with a stated advocacy orientation favoring higher infrastructure spending; its Report Card series has recurringly quantified an investment gap since its first edition.

dated.gap: Federal government difficulty controlling costs across a $750B+ procurement portfolio, including weapon-systems and IT acquisition regression 2023–2025
dated.sinceValue: 1990 (weapon systems acquisition; NASA acquisition management; DOD contract management lineage) / 2015 (IT acquisition and operations)
dated.evidence: GAO has designated DOD weapon systems acquisition and NASA acquisition management as high risk since 1990, and identified 'Improving the Management of IT Acquisitions and Operations' as a new high-risk area in its 2015 list [web:6][web:31][web:35][web:29].

dated.gap: VA electronic health record modernization, estimated at $49.8B in life-cycle costs, deployed to only six of 160+ locations as of December 2024
dated.sinceValue: 2015 (VA health care management, encompassing EHRM, added to GAO High-Risk List)
dated.evidence: GAO designated 'Managing Risks and Improving VA Health Care' a high-risk area in 2015, later citing EHRM implementation challenges as part of that designation [web:32][web:36][web:39][web:3].

dated.gap: FAA operational risk assessment found 51 of 138 air traffic control systems unsustainable and 54 more potentially unsustainable
dated.evidence: GAO's September 2024 report reported FAA's own 2023 determination that 51 of 138 systems are unsustainable, but no earlier official assessment naming ATC system unsustainability as a standing shortfall was located [web:53][web:56].

dated.gap: The February 2025 high-risk list contains thirty-eight areas covering continuously delivered public services (VA health care, Medicare/Medicaid, medical products oversight, public health emergency leadership, tribal programs)
dated.sinceValue: 1990 (Medicare); 2003 (Medicaid); 2015 (VA health care); 1990 (medical products oversight lineage); 2022 (HHS leadership/coordination of public health emergencies); 2017 (federal programs serving tribes)
dated.evidence: GAO added Medicare to its High-Risk List in 1990 and Medicaid in 2003; VA health care was designated in 2015; HHS leadership and coordination of public health emergencies was added in January 2022; programs serving tribes and their members were added in 2017 [web:40][web:32][web:99][web:44].

dated.gap: Twenty of the thirty-eight high-risk areas are on the list in part because of skills gaps or inadequate staffing
dated.evidence: GAO first designated strategic human capital management, the skills-gap issue underlying many high-risk areas, as high risk in 2001 [web:41][web:45].

dated.gap: FDA conducted an average of 917 foreign food safety inspections a year over FY2018–2023, about 5% of its 19,200 annual target
dated.evidence: The Food Safety Modernization Act, enacted in 2011, set the statutory ramp to an annual target of 19,200 foreign facility inspections that FDA has never approached [web:80][web:83].

dated.gap: 53% of public schools reported understaffing entering 2022–23; completions of teacher-prep programmes fell 20% from 2012–13 to 2019–20
Environmental impact statements run well past CEQ's recommended page limits; draft EISs averaged 575 pages for 2013–2018 actions
dated.evidence: GAO's April 2014 report on NEPA found that federal agencies lacked reliable data on time frames and document length, first officially flagging the EIS length problem that CEQ's later page-limit rule sought to address [web:88][web:95].

dated.gap: Fisheries management limited by assessment coverage: only 364 of 506 stocks had known overfishing status and 263 known overfished status (2023 report to Congress)
dated.evidence: NOAA Fisheries has reported on the status of U.S. fisheries, including unknown-status stocks, since 1996 under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act's statutory reporting requirement [web:57].

dated.gap: Low-income and historically redlined neighborhoods face up to 12°F hotter heatwave temperatures and greater flood risk; adaptive capacity unevenly distributed
Access to civil justice ranks 112th of 143 countries in the 2025 Rule of Law Index, against 27th overall
dated.evidence: The World Justice Project's Rule of Law Index, which separately scores 'accessibility and affordability of civil justice,' began its current comparable annual ranking methodology in 2015 [web:98][web:100][web:104].
dated.orientationNote: The World Justice Project is a rule-of-law advocacy and research organization; no official U.S. government body independently dates when civil-justice-access weakness was first identified.

dated.gap: Uncorrected age-adjusted death rates understate deaths by 34% for non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native population and 3% for Hispanic/Asian populations due to death-certificate race misclassification
dated.evidence: NCHS's 1999 report 'Quality of Death Rates by Race and Hispanic Origin' first formally documented systematic misclassification of race and Hispanic origin on U.S. death certificates as a measurable, uncorrected data-quality problem [web:87].
